headline: PM Tarique outlines 3-R strategy to rebuild Bangladesh in UNGA address
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman addressed the 81st UN General Assembly, detailing Bangladesh's 3-R strategy for recovery, restoration, and reconstruction after years of 'fascist rule'. He emphasized democracy, economic growth, and women's empowerment.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman addressed the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, outlining Bangladesh's '3-R strategy' – recovery, restoration, and reconstruction. This strategy aims to repair the nation after more than one and a half decades of 'fascist rule and exploitation'.

Rahman stated that Bangladesh is now embarking on the path of democracy, having freed itself from enforced disappearances, killings, abductions, corruption, looting, and money laundering. He highlighted an 'immense horizon of possibilities' that has opened for the country.

His government has begun implementing extensive programs to transform Bangladesh's working-age population into skilled human resources, leveraging the demographic dividend. Measures are in place to create widespread employment opportunities and develop Bangladesh as a 'manufacturing hub'.

The government has allocated US$50 million in the current fiscal year to support young entrepreneurs, researchers, and innovators in start-up initiatives. The Prime Minister also emphasized women's empowerment, placing women at the forefront of all government plans for socio-economic transformation.

Priorities include women's education, employment, and entrepreneurship, with expanded opportunities for cash financing, particularly in small and medium-sized industries. Free education up to the undergraduate level has also been made available for women.

The government aims to ensure not only electoral democracy but also the democratization of the economy, ensuring economic growth and prosperity reach every family and citizen. To this end, support programs like the Family Card, Farmers' Card, Sports Card, and e-Health Card have been introduced for economically disadvantaged people.

The Family Card, issued in the name of the female head of each household, symbolizes women's economic empowerment. Rahman also noted that 73 percent of the government's 31-point program, presented before the national election, directly aligns with the UN Sustainable Development Goals' 'Leave No One Behind' theme.

Special importance has been given to education, health, and sports, with the highest-ever budget allocation for the education sector. Plans include gradually increasing education spending to 5 percent of GDP within the next five years, focusing on technical and practical education.

To boost school enrollment and improve education quality, primary students receive free school bags, uniforms, and midday meals. Sports has also been included as a subject in the education curriculum for the first time, aiming to establish it as a profession, evidenced by a recent nationwide football tournament with over two million participants.

Addressing the international situation, the Prime Minister called for resolving conflicts through dialogue, diplomatic processes, and mutual cooperation. He highlighted that human-made conflicts create unrest, displacement, humanitarian crises, and severe pressure on the global economy, energy security, and supply systems.

headline_marked: [[PM, UN chief discuss Rohingya crisis, climate change]] at UN General Assembly
headline: PM, UN chief discuss Rohingya crisis, climate change at UN General Assembly
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres met at the UN headquarters to address the Rohingya crisis and climate change impacts. They also discussed Bangladesh-UN cooperation and global issues.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres held a meeting on Thursday. They discussed finding a sustainable solution to the Rohingya crisis and addressing the adverse impacts of climate change.
The discussion took place on the 27th floor of the UN Secretariat Building at the UN headquarters. This meeting was held on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

Key topics included Bangladesh-UN cooperation, various important global and regional issues, and matters of mutual interest. They also exchanged views on Bangladesh's development journey and its contributions to UN peace and security efforts.

PM Rahman emphasized the importance of UN cooperation and support for Bangladesh's priorities and national interests. He reaffirmed Bangladesh's commitment to multilateralism, international cooperation, peace, and sustainable development.

The UN Secretary-General underscored the need to further advance the longstanding cooperation between Bangladesh and the United Nations. Both leaders expressed their commitment to continue mutual cooperation and work closely on common global challenges.
